themes_detail.label: Asbestos Crisis Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints surged dramatically this week to 3 complaints in a single 2-week period vs. a baseline of 0.1 complaints weekly over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% spike—suggesting either discovery of contaminated sites or building demolition/renovation activity triggering exposure concerns in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill.
evidence: 3 asbestos complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
z-score of 8.69 indicates severe statistical anomaly
320 building permits filed in last 90 days (224 alterations, 7 full demolitions) may indicate renovation/demolition triggering asbestos exposure
reporting_angles: Which specific buildings or sites are generating asbestos complaints? Are residents being properly notified?
Cross-reference the 3 complaints with DOB demolition/major alteration permits—are contractors following asbestos abatement protocols?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped 327% last week to 8 complaints vs. a 1.9 weekly average over 8 weeks, marking a sharp rise in unauthorized signage, graffiti, or advertisements across the district.
evidence: 8 illegal posting complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (327% increase)
z-score of 4.49 indicates statistically significant spike
Aligns with community board requests for enhanced park safety and environmental improvements
reporting_angles: What types of illegal postings are proliferating? Are they gang tags, commercial advertisements, or political campaign materials?
Is this a coordinated effort or organic increase? Are enforcement responses keeping pace with complaints?

themes_detail.label: Curb & Street Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints surged 211% last week to 7 complaints vs. a 2.2 weekly baseline, while street condition complaints remain consistently high at 1131 over 90 days, pointing to accelerating pavement and infrastructure decay in the district.
evidence: Curb condition complaints: 7 last week vs. 2.2 weekly average (211% spike, z-score 7.18)
Street condition complaints: 1131 total over 90 days (third-highest complaint type)
7 full demolitions in last 90 days may be contributing to curb damage
reporting_angles: Is the spike in curb complaints tied to construction/demolition activity, or is it a sign of deferred maintenance?
Which streets or neighborhoods are most affected? Are pothole repair requests being met?

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints jumped 256% to 20 complaints over the 2-week period vs. a 5.6 weekly average, significantly above residential noise complaints (1042 total over 90 days), suggesting new commercial activity or expansion in the district.
evidence: 20 commercial noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.6 weekly average (256% increase, z-score 4.34)
44 new building permits filed in last 90 days may indicate new commercial spaces opening
Community board budget requests include park safety enhancement, suggesting residents perceive safety/quality of life concerns
reporting_angles: Which businesses or construction sites are generating the spike in commercial noise?
Are new commercial establishments (restaurants, bars, gyms) opening without proper soundproofing or permit compliance?

themes_detail.label: Infrastructure Maintenance Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Over the last 2 weeks, complaints for litter baskets (1100% spike to 3 vs. 0.2 baseline), curb condition (211% spike), and new tree requests (700% spike to 3 vs. 0.4 baseline) suggest residents are signaling a broader breakdown in street-level infrastructure maintenance and public realm upkeep.
evidence: Litter basket complaints: 3 (2 weeks ago) vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
New tree requests: 3 (last week) vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 5.42)
Community board repeatedly requests park/building improvements and new/expanded park amenities—unsolved problem
reporting_angles: Is the city cutting back on routine sanitation and maintenance staff in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill?
Do residents perceive the district as being neglected compared to other neighborhoods? Interview community board members about funding gaps.
